name: Seppa
description: District headquarters of East Kameng, situated on the banks of the Kameng River at about 363 m elevation. Scenic valley town with riverside views, local Nyishi markets, and a base for exploring the three valleys and nearby hill stations. Formerly known as Sepla meaning marshy land.
facts: Helipad in the heart of town

name: Bameng
description: Cool hill station and circle headquarters about 48 km north of Seppa. Offers panoramic views of valleys, traditional Nyishi villages, and sight of the snow-peaked Gorichaan mountain. Ideal for quiet escapes amid misty hills and agricultural landscapes.
facts: Cool climate like a hill station

name: Chayangtajo
description: Scenic high-altitude hill station and circle HQ about 81 km from Seppa, famous for views of the snow-peaked Gorichaan mountain. Features cardamom plantations, rice terraces, mountain streams, and authentic Nyishi longhouses in a misty valley setting at around 1,500 m.
facts: Famous for Gorichaan snow peak views

name: Pappu Valley (Lumdung)
description: Spectacular valley along the meandering Pappu River about 21 km from Seppa, named for its snake-like curvy streams. Vast paddy fields, green summer landscapes, and famous for migratory birds in winter at Lumdung. Promoted for eco-tourism including potential paragliding.
facts: Meandering Pappu River with paddy fields
Lumdung known for winter migratory birds
Part of the Three Valleys attraction

name: Kameng River (Seppa section)
description: Major river flowing through East Kameng, popular for angling and fishing in winter near Seppa (permission required from district administration). Offers scenic river views, potential white-water rafting in gorges, and forms the lifeline of the district with turquoise waters amid hills.
facts: Good angling spot in winter with permit

name: Khenewa
description: Scenic valley and circle area with verdant hills, river views, and open spaces. Misty winters add to the beauty; popular for landscape photography, peaceful walks, and local markets amid Nyishi cultural settings. Offbeat stop near Bameng.
facts: Ideal for photography and quiet exploration

name: Lada
description: Remote mountain settlement in the western part of the district, embraced by forests, steep hills, and babbling brooks. Offers peace, privacy, and tribal traditions with pristine landscapes suitable for trekking and photography away from main circuits.

name: Gorichaan Viewpoint (from Bameng/Chayangtajo)
description: Snow-peaked mountain visible from Bameng and Chayangtajo hill stations in East Kameng. Locally significant and a highlight of the area’s high-altitude scenery; best viewed on clear days from elevated points in the district.
facts: Best on clear winter or post-monsoon days
